# FLX-3303: an INT expose column is mapped onto a source that is not always a whole number

**Family:** seam/conformance (the 3000 band)

KERNEL-SPEC §9 renders an INT column as a JSON integer. A scenario-driven emit decides at plan time, from the declarations alone, whether the source mapped onto an INT column is always a whole number: one of the integer scalars (subject.ordinal, event.time, moment.firstTime, moment.lastTime, moment.eventCount), or an attribute, trait or payload field whose every declared family draws only whole numbers (a rate count, a bounded normal at scale 0, a constant whole number). Any other source could put a fraction, a string or a bool into the column, and whether a run then failed would depend on which values it drew, so the run is refused before a row exists. Map the column onto a whole-number source, or declare it DECIMAL(p,s), which renders an exact number at its declared scale.
